first_bad: 24488b4 host: identify ports by VID/PID on every platform
last_good: ea13eb8 tools: flash Track A through the path that works on every host
means: The bisect is sound as a bisect and its conclusion is NOT 'this commit introduced the defect'. It is 'this commit stopped masking it'. A pre-existing defect that a per-discovery board reset was hiding fits every observation here and is the more likely reading, because a change to host-side port identification has no plausible route to mid-stream frame loss at a reading client.
next_test: On 24488b4, reset the board before each run. If it goes clean, the reset was the mask and the defect is older than the bisect range.
not_claimed: That 24488b4 is innocent. Only that 'first bad commit' and 'cause' have come apart here.
the_caveat: 24488b4 REMOVED A BOARD RESET FROM DISCOVERY. Before it, find_all_ports() probed on POSIX - 'the control port is the one that answers h' - and probing opens the programming port, which asserts NRSTB and resets the board. Its own message says so. After it, discovery matches VID/PID and never opens that port. So every GOOD commit in this bisect ran against a board that had just been reset, and every BAD one did not.
